# INvenTree Data User Compliance Checklist

Use this checklist before requesting data, throughout the project, and before submitting any resulting output. It is based on the INvenTree collaboration and data-sharing policy provided.

## 1. Before requesting or accessing data

- [ ] Email all the data owners and data steward with a data request.
- [ ] Comply with data originator specified restrictions on data use (for both public and private datasets)
- [ ] Verify with the data originator the level of data that can be made public during eventual publication of the work

## 2. During project development (iterative process)

- [ ] Use a reproducible workflow with version control from the beginning of the project.
- [ ] Update project participants regularly as the project evolves (on conceptual, analytical and writing developments)
- [ ] Discuss rough authorship guidelines at the start of the project.

## 3. Project first draft stage

- [ ] Share the draft of the output (e.g., manuscript, report, etc) with all members of the project, including all data originators, for feedback
- [ ] Recognise meaningful contributions appropriately, including dataset access, research-question formulation, analysis, and manuscript preparation.

## 4. Before making any output public

- [ ] Circulate the final draft to all project participants before submission. Participants should be given a reasonable timeline (2-3 weeks) to provide feedback.
- [ ] Ensure compliance with the agreed upon restrictions for each dataset
- [ ] Confirm that data originators have been appropriately invited to collaborate and/or offered appropriate authorship where warranted.
- [ ] Confirm that the output follows the project's reproducible-workflow practices.
- [ ] Confirm that required INvenTree attribution/citation is included.

## 5. After the output is public

- [ ] Notify the INvenTree Team of outputs arising from INvenTree data or projects, including reports, preprints, and publications.
- [ ] Continue to protect private data from unauthorised disclosure, copying, transfer, or third-party access.
